messages.subject: Recombination Fractions >> 0.5
parts:
Karl & other R/qtl discussion group members:  .

GBS was used to generate SNP markers for a soybean F4-derived RIL population of 211 individuals using the sequenced soybean genome (20 chrs) as the reference in Tassel for outputting a R/qtl ready data set.  

The *.bmp attachment shows the physical (bp) map locations of the outputted SNPs.  Obviously, there are soy chr regions (gaps) where the mated parents are monomorphic.

However, the problem that prompted this (my) e-mail is when the est.rf and est.map functions were used to derive a genetic map (kosambi cM) . 

Many rf values for SNP pairs GREATLY exceed the theoretical expectation of 0.5 (see attached *.bmp file of LOD vs rf).  There is apparently a lot of corrective work that must be done to get this populations plot of LOD vs rf to the kind shown in Karl's Figure 10 (see attached *.bmp file) in his Guide to Mapping... tutorial). 

So my first question is this:  Is it common for GBS to generate a large number of SNPs in which the parental allele phase inversed (assuming that this is the cause of the rf values greater than the theoretical max of 0.5?  

SNP pairs with rf >>> 0.5 are not a problem so long as the SNP Pair Members are on different chromosome.  However, it is (a big) problem when the SNP pair members are on the SAME chromosome.  Indeed, when rf values for the SNP pairs on a given chr are much greater than 0.4999....  the chr cM map inflation can be huge - see *.bmp file with this population's genetic map).    

I recognize that sampling error occurs when one is estimating rf values for any given RIL population, even when the true SNP pair rf value is close to theoretical max pf 0.5, but rf estimates excessively greater than 0.5 translate into huge cM distances.

So my second question is this:  Can one somehow restrict same chromosome SNP pairs to a max of (say) 0.4999999 to resolve this sampling error problem when rf values are converted to (kosambi) map function cM distances?     

If the answer to that 2nd question is NO, then I have a third question:

Is there a convenient R/qtl code that can be used to EXTRACT  from the all possible SNP pair rf matrix JUST THOSE SNPs that are:
(1) ONLY on a given specified chromosome, AND THEN (not and/or) 
(2) ONLY same-specified chromosome SNP pairs that have rf values > 0.4999. 

If there are a lot of SNPs that need corrective work (as Karl notes in his Guide tutorial) then I really need a short list of SNPs to get started on that work!  Any suggested short-cut R/qtl code to get the corrective work done quicker would also be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Recombination Fractions >> 0.5
parts:
It doesn't sound like a sampling error problem. Usually, when you're getting rf >> 0.5, the problem is that the genotypes that you thought were AA are really BB and vice versa.

karl
